To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fuzzy Bayesian network is a general representation formalism for hybrid Bayesian networks in the form of two approximate representations, which are called FBN form-I and form II.

the fuzzy Bayesian network is a new formalism for representing, inferring, and learning general hybrid Bayesian networks and that inference and learning with FBN can be done efficiently by extending the junction tree inference algorithms and the expectation-maximization algorithm, respectively.

fuzzy Bayesian networks (FBNs) provide a general formalism to represent, infer and learn with general hybrid Bayesian Networks, and that the FBN form-II, which is a finer approximate representation of hybrid Bayesian networks than the FBN form-I, can be applied to solve a wide range of problems in the fields of machine learning, data mining, knowledge discovery and data fusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general formalism of fuzzy Bayesian networks, which is a generalization of hybrid Bayesian networks, and a general framework for representation, inference, and learning of such networks.
general representation, inference and hybrid learning of fuzzy Bayesian networks.
the representation of hybrid Bayesian networks by fuzzy Bayesian networks and the inference, learning and decision-making in the resulting fuzzy Bayesian networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FBN formalism provides a general framework for representation, inference, and learning with hybrid Bayesian networks in a way that is consistent with the discrete Bayesian networks and that the FBN is more general than the hybrid Bayesian networks.
the proposed general formalism for hybrid Bayesian network representation and inference is an effective way to deal with general hybrid Bayesian network problems.
fuzzy Bayesian networks provide an alternative general formalism for representing, inferring and learning with hybrid Bayesian networks, but the inference is still exact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a general formalism, called fuzzy Bayesian networks, for representing, reasoning and learning with general (hybrid) Bayesian networks.
we propose a new formalism, called FBN, to approximate a general hybrid Bayesian network by a discrete Bayesian network with latent discrete variables and CG or CGR approximations.
we have developed the FBN formalism, the inference algorithms for FBNs, and the EM algorithm for learning FBNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a general hybrid Bayesian network can be approximated by an equivalent FBN, in which all the continuous and discrete variables can be replaced by discrete variables, and inference can be done exactly by the junction tree algorithm, which is the fastest inference algorithm for discrete networks.

a hybrid Bayesian network can be fuzzified into a fuzzy Bayesian network (form-I or form-II), and inference and learning with fuzzy Bayesian networks is more efficient than inference and learning with hybrid Bayesian networks.
the FBN formalism is general and can be applied to any hybrid Bayesian network, and the inference and learning algorithms are general and can handle any type of hybrid Bayesian networks.
